explanations.answer: Every stone will be thrown down
explanations.explanation: Jesus says, “Not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.” The disciple was admiring the buildings, and Jesus answers with something totally different. I love how plain it is. No wiggle room, friend. Every. Single. Stone.

explanations.answer: They will be covered in gold
explanations.explanation: Gold never comes up in what Jesus says. He talks about stones and what happens to them. I once tried to dress up a plain cookie with extra glaze and it just looked like a plain cookie wearing a costume. Jesus's words are simpler than that: “Not one stone here will be left on another.”

explanations.answer: They will stand for all time
explanations.explanation: Jesus says the opposite. “Not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.” The disciple was looking at buildings that seemed solid. Jesus is looking at the same buildings and says they won't stay.

That's right. The four ask Him, “Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to be fulfilled?” They asked Him privately, on the Mount of Olives. Good questions, friend. I'd have asked them too, probably with flour on my face.

The four did ask. In Mark 13:4 they say, “Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to be fulfilled?” They ask about both the timing and the sign. That's a real question, asked right out loud.
Jesus begins with, “See to it that no one deceives you.” Out of everything He could open with, that's the first thing. I'd say that tells us how much it matters. Keep your eyes open, friend.
Flattery doesn't show up in this warning. Jesus says, “See to it that no one deceives you.” Flattery is just compliments, and I will take a few of those any day. Deception is the word Jesus uses.
Jesus doesn't mention anyone commanding them here. He says, “See to it that no one deceives you.” The warning is about being led astray. Someone bossing you around is a different problem entirely.

Jesus says, “When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed.” Wars and rumors of wars sound like exactly the time to panic, and He says don't. He gives them a reason too: “These things must happen, but the end is still to come.” That's a calm word for a loud time.

Jesus doesn't tell them to be silent. He says, “do not be alarmed.” Later in this same teaching He tells them to speak whatever they are given when they're arrested. These folks aren't being told to hush.
Idle isn't the word Jesus uses. He says, “do not be alarmed.” Staying calm is different from sitting around. He does say, “So be on your guard,” which is not a nap-on-the-couch kind of instruction.

Jesus says the opposite. After mentioning wars and rumors of wars, He says, “These things must happen, but the end is still to come.” So the wars come, and the end is still ahead. Hearing about wars doesn't mean the timer has gone off.
That's what Jesus says. “These things must happen, but the end is still to come.” The wars aren't the end. They're something that comes before it.

Jesus says, “These are the beginning of birth pains.” That's His picture for the nations rising against each other, the earthquakes and the famines. Birth pains are only the beginning of something, and He puts it that way. I like that it's a picture we can all follow.

explanations.answer: The first drops of a storm
explanations.explanation: A storm is a good picture, but it's not the one Jesus uses. He says, “These are the beginning of birth pains.” It's a different kind of picture, and it's His, so we stick with it.

explanations.answer: The first cracks in a wall
explanations.explanation: That one sounds like it could fit, since He did just talk about stones falling. But Jesus doesn't call the wars, earthquakes and famines cracks in a wall. He says, “These are the beginning of birth pains.”

Jesus says they'll stand there as witnesses, not as judges. His words are, “On My account you will stand before governors and kings as witnesses to them.” They're being handed over, not handed a gavel. Quite a switch from what you might expect.
Right. Jesus says, “On My account you will stand before governors and kings as witnesses to them.” Witnesses, not judges. They show up because of Him, and they speak about Him.

Jesus says, “And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.” Notice the word “first.” Something has to happen before the end, and it's a message going out to every nation. Big job. Good thing it's not mine to bake alone.
The law isn't what Jesus names. He says, “And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.” The word is gospel, and it goes to all the nations.
Psalms are lovely, but they're not what Jesus is talking about here. He says, “And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.” That's the message that has to go out first.

Jesus says, “for it will not be you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.” They don't have to rehearse in advance, because they speak whatever they are given at that time. I would still rehearse. Jesus gives them something better than a rehearsal.
Jesus doesn't mention an angel here. He says, “it will not be you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.” The Spirit is the one who speaks. Friend, that's the part to hold onto.

The elders aren't named in this part. Jesus says the disciples will be delivered to councils, but the one who speaks is the Holy Spirit. His words are, “it will not be you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.”
That's right. Jesus says, “You will be hated by everyone because of My name…” That's hard to hear, and He says it plainly. I think it's kind of Him to tell them ahead of time.

Jesus does say it. His words are, “You will be hated by everyone because of My name…” He tells them straight, before it happens. That's a hard line, so I'll just say it once, simply: it's a heavy one.

explanations.answer: The one who perseveres to the end
explanations.explanation: Jesus finishes that line with, “…the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.” Right after the hard word about being hated, He gives a promise. The promise is for the one who keeps going. Hold onto that one, friend.

explanations.answer: The one who is never arrested
explanations.explanation: Jesus says nothing like that. He actually tells the four they'll be arrested and handed over. The promise is, “…the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.”

explanations.answer: The one who knows the day
explanations.explanation: Knowing the day isn't what Jesus ties the promise to. He says, “…the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.” In fact, He says elsewhere that no one knows the day or the hour except the Father (Matthew 24:36). That's why my ovens stay ready.
Jesus says, “then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.” He means for them to move, and He says where. Judea is the region where they are. When Jesus says go, friend, it's time to go.
Jesus doesn't send them to the temple. He says, “let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.” They're told to flee, and the mountains are where they run.
Cities aren't the place Jesus names. He says, “let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.” The direction is out of there, toward the mountains.
Jesus says the opposite. His words are, “And let no one in the field return for his cloak.” No running back, no grabbing it first. When He says go, He means go.
That's right. Jesus says, “And let no one in the field return for his cloak.” The one in the field doesn't turn back. A cloak is a good thing to leave behind when you have somewhere to be.

Jesus says, “Pray that this will not occur in the winter.” He doesn't say why winter, so I'll only guess. I think running for the mountains in the cold sounds miserable. He tells them to pray about it, and that's a good model for us.
Spring isn't the season Jesus names. He says, “Pray that this will not occur in the winter.” He doesn't tell us why. He only tells them to pray.
Summer isn't the one. Jesus says, “Pray that this will not occur in the winter.” He tells them to pray about it, and winter is the season He names.
Jesus says, “But for the sake of the elect, whom He has chosen, He has cut them short.” The Lord is the one who does it. That's a gentle line after a heavy one. I think it's a comfort.
Jesus says the opposite. “…for the sake of the elect, whom He has chosen, He has cut them short.” The days get shorter, not longer. It's for the sake of the elect.
Jesus isn't hiding anything here. He says the Lord has cut those days short, and the reason is, “for the sake of the elect, whom He has chosen.” In fact, Jesus tells them all of this on purpose.
That's right. Jesus says, “If the Lord had not cut short those days, nobody would be saved.” Then He adds that the Lord has cut them short. That's a hard sentence with a kind turn at the end.
Jesus does say it. His words are, “If the Lord had not cut short those days, nobody would be saved.” The next thing He says is that the Lord has cut them short for the sake of the elect.
Jesus says the opposite. When someone says, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ His words are, “do not believe it.” No road trip to check, friend.
Right. Jesus says that if anyone says, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ then, “do not believe it.” He doesn't send them off to investigate. He just says don't believe it.

Jesus says, “to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” The word “even” tells you how strong these signs and wonders will look. Those are His words, so they're worth hearing twice. That's why He keeps warning them.
The scribes aren't named in this warning. Jesus says the false Christs and prophets will try “to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” The elect are the ones He names.
The Romans aren't mentioned in this part. Jesus says the false Christs and false prophets will try “to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” That's the group He names.
Jesus says, “So be on your guard; I have told you everything in advance.” He didn't leave them to be surprised. I think that's what a good teacher does. He tells them first.

explanations.answer: Sent an angel to guard them
explanations.explanation: Jesus doesn't mention an angel here. What He says is, “So be on your guard; I have told you everything in advance.” What He has done is tell them ahead of time.

Jesus doesn't promise that. He warns them they'll be arrested, beaten and hated. What He says is, “So be on your guard; I have told you everything in advance.” Telling them ahead is how He prepares them.
